newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes down on Thai squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes down on Thai squeeze.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended midday losses to close lower after sellers adjusted quotes to match falling prices in Thailand, traders said.

Some marginal buying and selling, mostly for short-covering, was seen in the local market on Thursday, said the dealers. The market remained under pressure from the steep fall in Thai rubber values due to the flotation of the baht, said traders.

At midday, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted August buyers of the benchmark RSS1 at 247 Malaysian/Singapore cents (98 U.S. cents) a kg, down 2.50 cents from Wednesday's close. August SMR20 was two cents off to 241.
Local prices looked set to end the week with another sharp fall on Friday as prices in Thailand were much lower, said traders in Malaysia.
"If we don't follow them, our goods can't catch up with their price," a rubber trader in Kuala Lumpur said.
Local dealers said that despite adjustments, the SMR20 was still at a premium of six to seven Malaysian/Singapore cents against the Thai TSR20 at midday.
They said Thai rubber traders were also transacting in US dollars to protect themselves against "real effects" of the baht's devaluation.
A check with Malaysian trading houses in the evening showed SMR20 being offered at 238/237 cents, SMR10 at 239/238, SMR5 at 252, SMR CV at 309/308, SMR L at 290 and drum latex at 205/204.
The INRO five-day average ended at 194.66 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 2 compared to 196.79 on July 2. -- By K. Baranee Krishnaan (603 275-6833) ($1-2.5240).
